blocks.text: How To Maintain Your Painted Surfaces for Long-Lasting Beauty

blocks.alt: A blue paint roller is being used to paint a white wall.

blocks.text: Maintaining a painting job is easier said than done. Many residential and commercial property owners don’t know how to keep a professional paint job looking fresh. Most wait for their surfaces to get dirty again and then just slap another layer of paint on to cover the stains.

blocks.text: Proper care and maintenance, however, can significantly extend the life of your painted surfaces while saving you money on another expensive professional paint job.

blocks.text: What To Do After Someone Paints Your House
If you want to keep the fresh look of your newly painted surface, here are ten simple tweaks, tricks, and tips to help you do just that.
blocks.html: If you want to keep the fresh look of your newly painted surface, here are ten simple tweaks, tricks, and tips to help you do just that.

blocks.text: Wipe Spills Immediately

Accidents happen all the time, especially if you have kids or pets. If someone spills something on your newly painted surface, wipe it off immediately. Colored liquids and substances can leave permanent stains if left for too long.
blocks.html: Accidents happen all the time, especially if you have kids or pets. If someone spills something on your newly painted surface, wipe it off immediately. Colored liquids and substances can leave permanent stains if left for too long.

blocks.text: Stay Away from Harsh Chemicals

Keep your bathroom cleaners off your painted surfaces. Better yet just stick with a simple soap and water. Painted surfaces are susceptible to peeling and chemical damage, so it’s best to avoid using harsh chemicals on them. A damp cloth is usually all you need to clean your painted surfaces.
blocks.html: Keep your bathroom cleaners off your painted surfaces. Better yet just stick with a simple soap and water. Painted surfaces are susceptible to peeling and chemical damage, so it’s best to avoid using harsh chemicals on them. A damp cloth is usually all you need to clean your painted surfaces.

blocks.text: Stick to Using Cloth

You might be tempted to use your trusty scrub brush or abrasive sponge when cleaning your painted surfaces. Try not to rely on these harsh cleaning tools, as they can leave scratches and damage your paint. As mentioned earlier, a damp cloth works wonders, but if the situation calls for a stronger force, only use the soft side of your sponge.

blocks.text: Schedule Regular Cleaning

Dust and dirt can make painted surfaces look dull and worn out. Regularly cleaning your walls with a soft cloth or sponge and a mild detergent can help keep their appearance. As mentioned earlier, avoid abrasive cleaners because they can chip the paint.

blocks.text: Address Moisture Issues

Moisture is a common enemy of painted surfaces. Ensure your property is well-ventilated and address any leaks or dampness promptly. In bathrooms and kitchens, exhaust fans are used to reduce moisture buildup, which can lead to peeling and mold growth.
blocks.html: Moisture is a common enemy of painted surfaces. Ensure your property is well-ventilated and address any leaks or dampness promptly. In bathrooms and kitchens, exhaust fans are used to reduce moisture buildup, which can lead to peeling and mold growth.

blocks.text: Touch-Up When Necessary

Minor nicks, scratches, and chips are inevitable over time. Address these imperfections as soon as they occur to prevent them from worsening. Keep some leftover paint from your project for quick touch-ups that blend seamlessly with the existing paint job.
blocks.html: Minor nicks, scratches, and chips are inevitable over time. Address these imperfections as soon as they occur to prevent them from worsening. Keep some leftover paint from your project for quick touch-ups that blend seamlessly with the existing paint job.

blocks.text: Use Protective Measures

In high-traffic areas, consider using protective measures to prevent damage to painted surfaces. Chair rails, wainscoting, or even clear wall protectors can shield walls from scuffs and dents. In commercial properties, you can use corner guards and wall bumpers to protect vulnerable areas.

Chair rails, wainscoting, or even clear wall protectors can shield walls from scuffs and dents. In commercial properties, you can use corner guards and wall bumpers to protect vulnerable areas.

blocks.text: Apply a Layer of Wax

Right after your paint dries, consider applying a thin layer of wax for added protection and shine. Waxes specifically formulated for painted surfaces can add a layer of durability and make cleaning easier. Some paint job companies offer this service as part of their post-paint maintenance package, so make sure to ask your contractor.

blocks.text: Maintain a Stable Indoor Environment

Extreme temperature fluctuations and humidity levels can affect the integrity of your paint. Keep indoor temperatures and humidity levels stable to prevent cracking, peeling, or blistering. Buying a dehumidifier is a sound investment to draw out excess moisture in the air and keep your paint longer if you live in a humid region.

blocks.text: Schedule Regular Inspections

Periodic inspections by a professional can help identify potential issues before they become significant problems. Professional maintenance services can offer valuable advice and perform necessary repairs to keep your painted surfaces in top condition.

blocks.text: Make Your Paint Job Last a Long Time

A professional paint job can enhance your property’s aesthetic appeal and value. By following these ten easy-to-follow tips, homeowners and commercial property owners can ensure that their newly painted surfaces remain beautiful and durable for years to come.
